Can we pass ```std::string& name``` instead?

Passing references is usually preferred over passing pointers, since references have to be initialized, and with pointers we have to check for `nullptr`

https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/reference_initialization.html
Done
Can we pass ```std::set<std::string>& interface``` instead?
Done

Can you add a small comment about what this class represents.

Do you want to represent the contents of a single EM config, or a config json file.
Config json files may contain multiple EM configs (can refer to json schemas here)
Done

We may want a comment here that `name` maps to `"Name"`
and same for other members which map directly to json properties.
Done

Should we rename `command` to `probe` or `probeStmt` since that is the property name used in the json aswell?

It could be helpful when reading code to have some hint at which json property this class member is representing.
Done
Can we rename this to `probeInterfaces` or similar since `interfaces` can mean a lot of things as a variable name.
Done
If we copy construct the `nlohmann::json` members of `ConfigRecord`, can we get rid of the `std::vector<nlohmann::json>` here?

Is this the `Name` field from the configuration file?

That looks wrong.

Nice to see we can get rid of all those checks since the config has already been validated 😊

The member will be copy-constructed, but the configuration has not changed and will not be changed by this class, right?

Done

I believe this is wrong since the `configurations` vector holds EM configs of which there may be more than one in a configuration file (see `loadConfigurations`)

Maybe reword to 
"ConfigRecord represents information about an EM Config"
Done

Maybe we should rename this to `class EMConfig` to match with the name of the json schema
in `schemas/global.json`.
I would like to stay with ConfigRecord, because it is a hint, that this is just a structure for processing, but not the actual configuration.

"extracted from an EM config"
